# Reference fixtures

These JSON files are generated by `scripts/generate_reference_fixtures.py`, which runs with `python3 -I`. They are committed so that the test suite needs no Python. The generator uses only implementations that share **no code** with the TypeScript engine.

| File | Contents | Source of truth |
|---|---|---|
| `decode-tables.json` | Value of every bit pattern of FP8 E4M3, E5M2, E4M3FNUZ, E5M2FNUZ, FP4 E2M1 (as float64 hex), plus every FP16 / BF16 pattern (as float32, base64) | `ml_dtypes` 0.6.0, NumPy |
| `rne-conversions.json` | Round-to-nearest-even conversions of edge, midpoint, near-midpoint and random inputs | `ml_dtypes` (FP8/FP4/FNUZ/BF16, from float32-representable inputs); NumPy `astype` (FP16/FP32 from float64) |
| `directed-rounding.json` | float64 → binary32 and → binary16 conversions, and binary32 add/mul, under all four IEEE rounding directions | `scripts/reference/ref.c` compiled with gcc `-frounding-math`, using `fesetround` (x86-64 SSE; libgcc soft-fp for `_Float16`) |
| `prng.json` | First 16 outputs of xoshiro128** for five seeds | reference C code from prng.di.unimi.it, in `ref.c` |
| `integer-quantization.json` | Affine INT8/INT4 quantization (symmetric/asymmetric; per-tensor/channel/group) and percentiles | independent NumPy implementation (`np.rint` = ties-to-even, `np.percentile` linear) |
| `dot-products.json` | Exact dot products and FP16/FP32 sequential accumulations | `fractions.Fraction`; NumPy float16/float32 scalars |

All floating-point values are stored as raw IEEE bit patterns in hexadecimal, so values are exact and NaN, ±Inf and −0 survive JSON.

## Regenerating

```bash
pip install numpy ml_dtypes   # versions are recorded in each file's "provenance" field
python3 -I scripts/generate_reference_fixtures.py
```

The generator uses a fixed NumPy seed (`default_rng(20261027)`). NumPy may change its random streams between major versions, so regenerated files can contain different random inputs. The tests remain valid for any regenerated set.

## Known reference-library behaviour

`ml_dtypes` 0.6.0 rounds float64 inputs to FP8 by way of float32, which can double-round. See `docs/NUMERICS.md` §8. The fixtures therefore use only float32-representable inputs for `ml_dtypes`. `ml_dtypes` also maps NaN to −0 for FP4 E2M1, where the result is implementation-defined; NaN inputs are therefore excluded from the FP4 cases.
